## Start with your volume

Every volume begins with **Lab 00**. Choose or restore your project, try the notebook, and see how the chapter labs build toward a final discussion. No previous saved progress is required.

{{< include config/lab-inventory.qmd >}}

Labs run as full pages in your browser, with the book's navigation. The first launch downloads the runtime and dependencies and may take a few minutes.

## What you will do

1. **Read and predict.** Meet the situation, see the learning goals and complete route, and predict a consequence before opening an investigation.
2. **Change and compare.** Change one condition and inspect the immediate feedback. Explain what improves, what costs more, and what remains uncertain.
3. **Capture and discuss.** Keep contrasting evidence, defend a recommendation or hold, and say what would change your mind. Download the discussion to submit through your course's usual system.

The book explains concepts, TinyTorch builds the machinery, these labs explore design trade-offs, and StaffML practices defending decisions. Each chapter lab develops its own concepts within your continuing project.

::: {.lab-guide}
<details>
<summary>Saving your work</summary>

Capturing keeps a comparison fixed while you continue experimenting. Saving a discussion is an explicit action; later changes can make that saved evidence stale. The Design Ledger can retain saved decisions when browser storage is available. Keep a downloaded report for a portable record, especially when storage is unavailable. Storage does not synchronize across devices or submit work to your instructor.

LLM assistance can help with hypotheses and drafting. Your claims still need support from the experiment, including its assumptions and limits. Calculation Notes explain the governing models when you want to dig deeper.

</details>
:::

::: {.lab-guide}
<details>
<summary>Local notebooks and hardware</summary>

Browser labs need no local installation. To modify a notebook or run it locally, install the repository dependencies:

```bash
python3 -m pip install -r labs/requirements.txt
python3 -m pip install -e mlsysim
cd labs
marimo run vol1/lab_00_introduction.py
```

Install dependencies and launch once while connected before relying on offline use. For a separate hands-on robotics experience, explore the [Volume IV Physical AI Hardware Studio](vol4/README.md).

</details>
:::
